items.followUp: Write any four characteristics of a suspension.

rubric.why: A solution is a homogeneous mixture.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a solution is homogeneous.

rubric.why: A solution consists of a solute dissolved in a solvent.
rubric.description: Names the two components of a solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both the solute and the solvent.

rubric.why: The proportions of solute and solvent can vary.
rubric.description: States that the composition of a solution is variable.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for indicating that the components may be present in different proportions.

rubric.why: Solution particles are evenly distributed and do not settle out.
rubric.description: Gives a further characteristic of the solution particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one stated property: particles are uniformly distributed, do not settle, or cannot be separated by ordinary filtration.

modelAnswer: A solution is a homogeneous mixture.
It consists of a solute and a solvent.
Its composition can vary; the solute and solvent may be present in different proportions.
The solute particles are uniformly distributed and do not settle out.

items.followUp: Define a mixture and give one example.

rubric.why: The elements in a compound are joined by chemical combination.
rubric.description: States that the elements are chemically combined.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this defining feature.

rubric.why: Compounds have elements in a fixed proportion.
rubric.description: States that the constituent elements occur in a fixed ratio.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the fixed proportion and giving a correct example, such as water (H2O) or sodium chloride (NaCl).

modelAnswer: A compound is a pure substance formed when two or more elements are chemically combined in a fixed ratio.
For example, water (H₂O) is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen.

items.followUp: Define mass number and give one example.

rubric.why: Atomic number is defined by the number of protons in the nucleus.
rubric.description: Defines atomic number using the number of protons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that atomic number is the number of protons in an atom's nucleus.

rubric.why: A correct element and its atomic number illustrate the definition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct element-number pair, such as carbon = 6, sodium = 11, or oxygen = 8.

modelAnswer: Atomic number is the number of protons in the nucleus of an atom.
For example, carbon has atomic number 6.

items.followUp: What is meant by organic chemistry?

rubric.why: Biochemistry is a branch of chemistry.
rubric.description: Identifies biochemistry as a branch of chemistry.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a branch or field of chemistry.

rubric.why: Biochemistry concerns the chemical substances and processes of living organisms.
rubric.description: Connects the subject to chemical substances or processes in living organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for referring to chemical substances, reactions, or processes in living organisms.

modelAnswer: Biochemistry is the branch of chemistry that deals with the chemical substances and processes occurring in living organisms.

items.followUp: Write the subshell electronic configuration of nitrogen, ¹⁴₇N.

rubric.why: A neutral carbon atom has six electrons to arrange in its subshells.
rubric.description: Recognises the number of electrons in a neutral carbon atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying carbon as having 6 electrons.

rubric.why: This is the correct subshell electronic configuration for carbon.

modelAnswer: Carbon has atomic number 6, so a neutral carbon atom has 6 electrons.

rubric.why: Canal rays consist of positively charged particles or ions.
rubric.description: Identifies canal rays as positively charged particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they are positive rays or positive ions.

rubric.why: In a discharge tube, canal rays pass through holes in the cathode.
rubric.description: States how canal rays pass through the cathode.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning passage through the perforated cathode.

modelAnswer: Canal rays are streams of positively charged particles (positive ions) produced in a discharge tube.
They pass through the holes in the cathode and are also called anode rays.

rubric.why: Atomic radius describes a distance associated with an atom.
rubric.description: Identifies atomic radius as a distance.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is a distance.

rubric.why: The textbook definition measures from the centre of the nucleus to the outermost electron shell.
rubric.description: Names the two points between which atomic radius is measured.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying the centre of the nucleus and the outermost electron shell.

modelAnswer: Atomic radius is the distance from the centre of an atom’s nucleus to its outermost electron shell.

items.followUp: What is meant by a group in the Modern Periodic Table?

rubric.why: A period is a horizontal row in the Modern Periodic Table.
rubric.description: Identifies the layout of a period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a period is a horizontal row.

rubric.why: Elements in the same period have the same number of occupied electron shells.
rubric.description: States the shared shell number of elements in a period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that elements in the same period have the same number of electron shells.

modelAnswer: A period is a horizontal row of elements in the Modern Periodic Table.
Elements in the same period have the same number of occupied electron shells.
